Amborella is a monotypic genus of understory shrubs or small trees endemic to the main island, Grande Terre , of New Caledonia in the southwest Pacific Ocean. [ 5 ] The genus is the only member of the family Amborellaceae and the order Amborellales and contains a single species , Amborella trichopoda . [ 6 ] Amborella is of great interest to plant systematists because molecular phylogenetic analyses consistently place it as the sister group to all other flowering plants ; as a result, it is critical for understanding angiosperm evolution. It is understood to be the most basal extant flowering plant, [ 7 ] and is one of several groups treated as " basal angiosperms ". [ 8 ]
